newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Nazi death camp survivor kidnapped in Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Nazi death camp survivor kidnapped in Colombia.

text.p: Liesalotte Nathan, a German who came to Colombia after surviving Nazi death camps in the Second World War, has been kidnapped, apparently by common criminals, German diplomatic sources said on Thursday.

The 75-year-old Nathan and her daughter Miriam, reported to be 32, were snatched from their home in north Bogota in late August, the diplomatic sources said, confirming accounts broadcast by a TV news programme on Wednesday evening.

Nathan was born in the city of Hindenburg in what was at the time part of Germany's eastern territories, now Poland. She survived the Nazi concentration camps of Bergen-Belsen and Auschwitz and left Europe to live in Colombia in 1947.

An official at the German Embassy said: "We don't have much information about Nathan. She only came to the embassy a few times in the last 40 years and did not appear to have mixed much with either the German or the Jewish community."
Neighbours told the Noticiero De Las Siete news programme the two women were seized by a group of men who came to their home on Aug. 24 claiming to be interested in buying a plot of land.

Police said on Thursday the kidnappers had not sent a ransom demand and they believed they were pressuring Nathan into signing over the deeds to her land. Five suspected members of the gang have been captured but two of the men were believed at large and were thought to be holding the women.

"This is quite a strange case. It appears the women were kidnapped by common criminals. There is not a lot the embassy can do in the matter because we have received no requests from relatives in Germany," an embassy official said.
Colombia has one of the highest kidnap rates in the world.
